first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly records that this segment-level tactic bought acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention and warned against generalizing it. Given the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, discounting into a price war is the tempting-but-wrong slot use. The two measured declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly causally linked, with onboarding completion upstream of activation; fixing the funnel entry addresses both, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom only. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers and do nothing for the SMB acquisition/activation gap, and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the one under attack. I am spending both verification pulls on the evidence base for my own choice rather than on the tactic I have already ruled out: memory_86 is the direct warrant for simplify_onboarding and I want the original record's effect size, segment breakdown, and whether 'time-to-value' was measured or inferred; memory_31 is 64 days old and may describe changes already shipped, in which case the remaining headroom is small and the consolidated summary would be overstating available lift. Key downstream risk to flag: cutting signup fields can strip the qualification data that routes enterprise prospects into the demo-request path (memory_44), converting a self-serve activation win into a loss in qualified pipeline — the exact metric the objective targets. The experiment must therefore be instrumented on downstream qualified-revenue and enterprise-routing quality, not just completion and first-week activation, and should exempt or preserve fields used for enterprise routing. Uncertainty retained: the consolidated memories are summaries whose confidence intervals and segment scope are not visible to me, the QoQ declines may have an external cause (competitor-driven mix shift in who is signing up) that no onboarding change will fix, and if verification shows memory_86's lift was small or already harvested I would switch this slot to activation_messaging rather than proceed. Running at standard scale rather than broad rollout so the enterprise-routing side effect can be caught before it is company-wide.
